title: Formal Taylor jet matrices, origin rank and rank-minor ideals
statement: Let $\sigma$ be a finite variable index set, $L$ a field, $s,t\in\mathbf N$, and $f_i\in L[[X_j:j\in\sigma]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] for $i=1,\ldots,s$. Write $E_t=\{\gamma\in\mathbf N^\sigma:|\gamma|\le t\}$ and $\nu!=\prod_j\nu_j!$, mapped to the coefficient ring. Using the iterated formal partial derivatives [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative], define the matrix [def-weil-matrix] $B_t(f)$ with row index $\delta\in E_t$ and column index $(i,\eta)\in\{1,\ldots,s\}\times E_t$ by $B_t(f)_{\delta,(i,\eta)}=\partial^{\delta-\eta}f_i/(\delta-\eta)!$ when $\eta\le\delta$, and zero otherwise. The reciprocal factorial is taken in $L$ and embedded as a constant series. Set $r_t(f)=\operatorname{rank}_L B_t(f)(0)$ and $J_t(f)=J_{r_t(f)+1}(B_t(f))$ [def-trf-minor-ideal]. Here the minor ideal of any matrix with finite row and column index types is defined by transporting both index types through their standard equivalences with finite ordinals and applying the recorded minor ideal. The auxiliary multi-index factorial is also defined over every commutative coefficient ring by the same product. Empty variable and generator sets, $t=0$, and oversized minors are included.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Definition 7.9, (7.12) and Definition 7.13, pp.265--266; extraction of the six existing helper definitions from the formal Hilbert-stratum theorem module.
